title: There are a lot of myths about early wakings. But not everything you ...
description: There are a lot of myths about early wakings. But not everything you hear is true. If your baby is waking up before you’re ready to start the day, you might be wondering what’s actually going on. Let’s clear a few things up 👇 ⏰ A later bedtime will always fix early wakings. FALSE: Bedtime timing goes both ways. Too late can cause overtiredness and make early wakings worse. Too early, and your child may have simply completed their night’s sleep by that early morning rise time. 🌅 Waking up before the desired rise time? Treat it like a night waking. TRUE:  Starting the day too early – turning on lights, that first morning feeding/breakfast – can reinforce a habitual early wake cycle. Keep the room dark and interactions minimal until the desired wake time. ☀️😴 Too much daytime sleep can cause early wakes. TRUE:  Napping too much or too little can both trigger early mornings – one eats into nighttime sleep, the other leads to overtiredness. 💤 The first nap being too early reinforces early wakes. TRUE: A too-early first nap can reinforce early rising by acting as an extension of nighttime sleep, teaching the body to keep waking early. 👶 How your baby falls asleep at bedtime has no effect on early wakings. FALSE: When babies are used to being helped to sleep, they’re more likely to fully wake during the early morning when sleep is lighter. With low sleep pressure at that hour, resettling is hard – and independent sleep skills can make a difference. 🌄 Early wakings usually have a quick fix. FALSE: Early wakings often involve multiple factors – schedule, environment, sleep habits, hunger – and solving them take time and patience. Tracking sleep patterns in Huckleberry can help you identify what’s going on and find the right path forward. Early wakings aren't a one-size-fits-all issue. Luckily, we’re here to help. #huckleberryapp
